newsitem.title: USA: MAPCO to buy back stock, split stock.
newsitem.headline: MAPCO to buy back stock, split stock.

text.p: MAPCO Inc said on Tuesday it would buy back up to 3.5 million shares, or 12 percent of its outstanding stock, and split its stock on a two-for-one basis as part of a plan to double earnings per share within the next five years.

"The plan is designed to increase operating profit to $450 million and double earnings per share within the next five years," Philip Baxter, MAPCO executive vice president and chief financial officer, said in a statement.
The so-called "Four-Point Plan" for earnings involves a growth strategy to help MAPCO develop a leading presence in targeted energy markets, the company said.
"The plan adopted by the board is balanced to provide near-term shareholder rewards while maintaining the financial flexibility to pursue strategic opportunities," Baxter said.

MAPCO said it would purchase about 12 percent of its 28.9 million shares outstanding in the open market. The repurchase follows the board's May 29 authorization to buy back up to 2.5 million shares, or five million after the split.
MAPCO said it recently changed its business strategy to become a leader in target energy markets.

"The cornerstone of our new growth strategy is the transition of the company from a segment-based operator of assets to an enterprise-wide marketer of products and services in targeted energy markets," James Barnes, MAPCO chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
To that effect, Barnes said the company's financial results as of the third quarter 1996 would be reported in four business units: pipeline, retail propane, refining and retail petroleum.

One of the first initiatives to be approved by the board was a $73 million investment over the next two years in the company's retail petroleum business, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Robert Sachse said.
This will involve the construction of 36 new MAPCO Express stores in Tennessee, Alaska and along Interstate Highways.
For the first half of 1996, the retail petroleum division reported operating profit of $14 million, up from $7 million for the same period last year, the company said.
MAPCO is the fourth largest retail propane marketer in the United States.
